articles.text: MĀMA: Xiǎo Yún na, zuótian kǎoshì kǎowán le, jīntian hái zài wūli máng shénme na?
MOTHER: Xiǎo Yún, your exams were over yesterday. What are you still working on here today?
XIǍO YÚN: Xiě jǐfēng xìn, zhèixiē xìn zǎo jiu gāi xiě le, jīntian yǒu yìdiǎnr shíjiān, wǒ xiǎng bǎ tāmen xiěwán.
XIǍO YÚN: Writing a few letters. I should have written them a long time ago. I have a little time today, so I wanted to get them written.
MĀMA: Gěi yéyede xìn xiěle méiyou? Yéye nàme téng nǐ, kuài gěi tā xiě fēng xìn ba!
MOTHER: Have you written grandfather? He's so fond of you, you really should write him a letter!
XIǍO YÚN: Shàngcì yéye lái xìn shuō, tāmen gōngsī qǐng tā qù bāng máng ne. Zhèijiàn shìr, nín zěnme xiǎng?
XIǍO YÚN: The last time grandfather wrote, he said that their company had asked him to go help out. What do you think of that?
MĀMA: Tāmen gōngsī xiǎng gēn wàiguó rén zuò shēngyi, qǐng yéye qù bāng máng, zhèijiàn shìr, wǒ shénme yě bú yuànyi shuō.
MOTHER: Their company wants to do business with foreigners, so they asked your grandfather to help out. I don't want to say anything about this.
XIǍO YÚN: Wèishénme ne?
XIǍO YÚN: Why?

MĀMA: Qiánxiē nián, tāmen gōngsīde rén shuō nǐ yéye, shuōde nàme nánting. Xiànzài tāmen yǒu wèntí le, yòu xiǎngdào nǐ yéye le. Suàn le ba, ràng tāmen kànzhe bàn ba. Wǒ bù xiǎng quàn nǐ yéye qù bāng zhèige máng. Niánjì dà le, hǎohāorde zài jiāli xiūxixiūxi bǐ shénme dōu hǎo.

MOTHER: A few years back, the people in the company were saying such awful things about your grandfather. But now, they go to him with their problems. The hell with it! Let them do what they like. I don't want to advise your grandfather to help them. When a person gets old, it's best for him to stay at home and get a lot of relaxation.
XIǍO YÚN: Mā, wǒ xiǎng yéye yídìng bù tóngyì nínde shuōfǎ. Guòqùde shìr yǐjīng guòqu le. Xiànzài yǒu rén qǐng tā bāng máng, zài shuō zhèixiē shìr duì guójiā yǒu hǎochu, tā yídìng huì qù zuòde.
XIǍO YÚN: Ma, I'm sure that grandfather wouldn't agree with that. What's over is over. Now someone asks him to help out, and besides, these things are good for the country. I'm sure he'll do it.
MĀMA: Wǒ yě zhīdao, nǐ yéye nèige rén zhǐ yào yǒu gōngzuò, bù guǎn duō nán, tā yě huì pīnmìng qù zuòde. Nǐ xiě xìnde shíhou, bié wàngle xiěshang, ràng tā bié tài lèi le, měitian shuì ge xiǎo wǔjiào.

MOTHER: I know that too. Your grandfather is the kind of person who, as long as there's a job, will knock himself out to do it, no matter how hard it is. When you write the letter, don't forget to write that he mustn't tire himself out too much, and to take a little noontime nap every day.
XIǍO YÚN: Hǎo. Xiěshang le. Nǎinai huì hǎohāor zhàogu yéyede. Nín fàngxīn hǎo le.
XIǍO YÚN: Okay. It's written. Grandma will take good care of grandfather. Don't you worry.
MĀMA: Èi! Hǎo le, wǒ yào chūqu mǎi dōngxi, nǐde xìn xiěwán le méiyou? Wǒ lái gěi ni jì.
MOTHER: (Sigh) Okay, I've got to go out to buy some things. Have you finished writing your letters? I'll mail them for you.
XIǍO YÚN: Zhèi sānfēng xìn xiěwán le, děng yíxiàr, wǒ tiēshang yóupiào. Hǎo, xiànzài hǎo le. Nín názǒu ba.
XIǍO YÚN: These three are finished. Wait a second while I put stamps on them. Okay, they're ready. Here they are.
MĀMA: Wǒ zǒu le.
MOTHER: I'm leaving.
XIǍO YÚN: Mā, nín zǎo diǎnr huílai!
XIǍO YÚN: Ma, don't be gone long!
